intro: Da Nang rewards visitors with long sandy beaches, a lively food scene and easy trips to nearby Hoi An. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram. The city has 19 local bus lines, all new and air-conditioned, with a flat 8,000 ₫ fare inside city limits.
Use the DanaBus app or danangbus.vn for routes. Avoid the look-alike danabus.vn site, which has outdated prices.
Taxis are reasonable. Mai Linh, Vinasun and Song Han are reliable. Grab is widely used and shows prices upfront.
Motorbike taxis (xe ôm) are cheap for short hops. Helmets are required by law, so insist the driver provides one.
Rent a scooter or 4-speed bike near Tran Cao Van. Driving is chaotic, so many visitors hire a car with a driver.
Electric bicycles need no licence and suit city travel. Walking works well along the beach and in central streets. No ferry serves the city.

bana_cable.name: Ba Na Hills Cable Car
bana_cable.price_text: About 900,000 VND adult return, combo ticket varies; check on the day
bana_cable.tip: Buy online ahead of time for a faster queue, and go early on weekdays to avoid crowds.

golden_bridge.name: Golden Bridge
golden_bridge.price_text: Included with Ba Na Hills entry
golden_bridge.hours: Within Ba Na Hills opening hours
golden_bridge.tip: Arrive before 09:00 for photos without the big crowds.

dragon_bridge.name: Dragon Bridge, Da Nang
dragon_bridge.hours: Open all day; fire and water show on weekend nights
dragon_bridge.tip: Stand on the riverbank near the bridge end for the best view of the fire and water show.

lady_buddha.name: Lady Buddha
lady_buddha.tip: Dress modestly for the pagoda, and bring water as the steps are steep.

hoi_an_old_town.name: Hoi An Old Town
hoi_an_old_town.price_text: About 120,000 VND ticket for old town sites; check current rate
hoi_an_old_town.hours: Ticketed sites roughly 07:30–21:30; streets open all day
hoi_an_old_town.tip: Visit in the early morning or after dark when the lantern-lit streets are quiet.

my_khe.name: My Khe Beach
my_khe.price_text: Free; sunbed rental around 100,000 VND per set
my_khe.hours: Open all day; lifeguards in season
my_khe.tip: Swim between the lifeguard flags and ask locals about current conditions before entering the water.

an_bang.name: An Bang Beach
an_bang.tip: Quieter than My Khe, so good for relaxed afternoons with local seafood nearby.

asia_park.name: Asia Park
asia_park.price_text: Roughly 300,000 VND entry (estimate); check on the day
asia_park.tip: Buy the ticket online to skip the queue and check whether rides are included.

da_nang_bay.name: Da Nang Bay
da_nang_bay.price_text: Varies by boat tour; check on the day
da_nang_bay.hours: Boats usually run daytime and evening
da_nang_bay.tip: Book a short evening bay cruise for city lights from the water.

basket_boat.name: Hoi An Basket Boat
basket_boat.price_text: Roughly 120,000 VND per ride (estimate); haggle lightly
basket_boat.tip: Agree on the price and ride length before you board the boat.

night_market.name: Hoi An Night Market
night_market.price_text: Free to walk; food and shopping extra
night_market.tip: Try local dishes from small stalls and keep cash in small notes.

japanese_bridge.name: Japanese Covered Bridge
japanese_bridge.price_text: Often covered by Old Town ticket; check on the day
japanese_bridge.tip: Visit at dusk for lantern reflections, but expect crowds.

cham_museum.name: Museum of Cham Sculpture
cham_museum.price_text: About 60,000 VND (estimate); check on the day
cham_museum.tip: Allow 60 to 90 minutes and pick up the English labels at the entrance.

sun_world.name: Sun World Ba Na Hills
sun_world.price_text: Included with Ba Na Hills entry
sun_world.hours: Within Ba Na Hills opening hours
sun_world.tip: Plan your day around the Golden Bridge and the French Village.

vinwonders.name: VinWonders Nam Hoi An
vinwonders.price_text: Roughly 800,000 VND (estimate); check on the day
vinwonders.tip: Buy the ticket online and check which rides are included.

han_market.name: Han Market
han_market.tip: Try local breakfast dishes early and bargain politely for fruit.

son_tra_viewpoint.name: Son Tra Peninsula viewpoint
son_tra_viewpoint.tip: Drive or take a taxi up the peninsula and watch the sea from the lookout points.

tran_cao_van.name: Tran Cao Van food street
tran_cao_van.tip: Ask for local dishes at small plastic-stool stalls for the most authentic food.

hoi_an_cooking.name: Hoi An cooking class
hoi_an_cooking.price_text: Roughly 350,000 to 550,000 VND per person (estimate); check on the day
hoi_an_cooking.tip: Book a class that includes a market visit and a meal.

stays.why: Closest to the sand and the seafront walk. Many resorts and mid-range hotels. Good base for beach days.
The city centre, near the Dragon Bridge, Han Market and most restaurants. Easy bus and taxi links.
Quiet, green and near the sea. Few shops nearby, so plan on taxis or Grab for dinner. Best for resorts.
Budget guesthouses and cafés. Popular with backpackers and the place to rent a scooter or bike.

food: Try mì Quảng, the local turmeric noodle dish with a little broth, and bánh xèo, the crispy pancake.
Han Market is the easiest place to sample fresh seafood and local snacks in one visit.
Eat at busy local stalls. Pick the places with a queue of locals and plastic stools.
Seafood restaurants along the beach road are good for dinner. Check prices on the menu before ordering.
Ask for water and ice carefully. Stick to bottled water if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Ba Na Hills: a mountain resort with a long cable car ride. Check prices and opening times on the day.
Hoi An: an old trading town about 45 minutes away by car or taxi, depending on traffic. Good for a half-day or evening.
Marble Mountains: stone caves and small temples close to the beach. Easy to add to a half-day, with a taxi or bike.
